analysis: Examined the test-only file provider-swift/Tests/ClusterSupervisionChecks/main.swift (base lines 1-450; head lines 1-414 visible). The head change (lines 248-330) adds model-free checks only. Lines 248-252 check the pairing-keyed update slot. Lines 255-331 check the ClusterPairUpdate partner-state machine: wait until the partner has staged and drained; give up on a partner failure, a different target or disabled auto-update; treat stale, silent or unreachable partners as cannotCoordinate; and decode unknown phases as checking, never ready. They also check request take-once semantics, the one-hour drop, and the progress file round trip. No production source is included, so the security behavior of ClusterPairUpdate is not verified here. Unverified points for integration: how the partner progress is transported between Macs and whether it is authenticated; a forged or spoofed partner message could affect update timing or force a single-Mac update (availability only, TB-002/TB-003 adjacent). Also unverified are the file permissions on service-update-request.json and service-update.json, which a same-UID process could write to trigger 'darkbloom update' (similar to TB-012 same-UID concerns), and whether the update path still verifies release hashes. The tests mention hashMismatch as a partner failure, suggesting staging verifies hashes, but this is not proven. No findings because the changes are tests; a test file cannot itself introduce a regression. The threat model may need a TB entry for cluster pair update coordination once the implementation is reviewed.
